Q17001405.label: Thirty-second Amendment of the Constitution Bill 2013
Q17001405.desc: To abolish the Seanad, the upper house of the Oireachtas
aliases: Proposed 32nd Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q17001405.wiki: Thirty-second Amendment of the Constitution Bill 2013
Q17001405.summary: The Thirty-second Amendment of the Constitution Bill 2013 was a proposal to amend the Constitution of Ireland to abolish Seanad Éireann, the upper house of the Irish parliament, the Oireachtas. The proposal was rejected by the electorate in a referendum on 4 October 2013 by 51.7% voting against to 48.3% in favour.

Q108601789.label: We Continue the Change
Q108601789.summary: We Continue the Change, sometimes translated as Change Continues or Let's Pursue Change, is a centrist, anti-corruption political party and formerly an electoral alliance in Bulgaria founded by Kiril Petkov and Assen Vassilev. It was founded ahead of the November 2021 election. The party was officially registered on 15 April. The party was a ruling party in Bulgaria during the periods of Kiril Petkov's government and as part of the PP-DB alliance in the Nikolai Denkov government.

Q4128701.label: 1989 Soviet Union legislative election
Q4128701.desc: legislative election in the Soviet Union
Q4128701.summary: Legislative elections were held in the Soviet Union on 26 March 1989 to elect members of the Congress of People's Deputies, with run-offs on 2, 9 and 20 April and 14 and 23 May. They were the first partially free nationwide elections held in the Soviet Union, and would be the last national elections held in that country before its dissolution in 1991.

Q834493.label: Chinese Revolutionary Party
Q834493.desc: Political party of the Republic of China
Q834493.summary: The Kuomintang (KMT) is a major political party in the Republic of China (Taiwan). It was the sole ruling party of China from 1928 to 1949 until its relocation to Taiwan, and in Taiwan ruled under martial law until 1987. The KMT is a centre-right to right-wing party and the largest in the Pan-Blue Coalition, one of Taiwan's two main political groups. Its primary rival is the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), the largest party in the Pan-Green Coalition. As of 2025, the KMT is the largest single party in the Legislative Yuan and is chaired by Cheng Li-wun.

Q530365.label: Rikken Minseitō
Q530365.desc: political party in the Empire of Japan
Q530365.summary: The Constitutional Democratic Party was one of the main political parties in pre-war Empire of Japan. Commonly known as the Minseitō, it was the main rival to the Rikken Seiyūkai.

Q6102461.label: Escobar Rebellion
Q6102461.desc: conflict in northern Mexico in 1929 during the Maximato
Q6102461.img: Mexican Army In Trenches Siege of Naco Sonora 1929.JPG
Q6102461.summary: The Escobar Rebellion was a conflict in northern Mexico in 1929 during the Maximato, between the government forces of President Emilio Portes Gil and rebel forces under the command of General José Gonzalo Escobar. After some initial success in taking over several key cities in the northern half of the country, the Escobar rebels were decisively defeated in a major battle at Jiménez, Chihuahua, and were eventually swept aside by the advancing government forces under the command of General Calles.

Q15310269.label: Battle of Beda Fomm
Q15310269.desc: battle as part of Operation Compass during World War II
Q15310269.summary: The Battle of Beda Fomm took place following the rapid British advance during Operation Compass. The Italian 10th Army was forced to evacuate Cyrenaica, the eastern province of Libya. In late January, the British learned that the Italians were retreating along the Litoranea Balbo from Benghazi. The 7th Armoured Division was dispatched to intercept the remnants of the 10th Army by moving through the desert, south of the Jebel Akhdar via Msus and Antelat as the 6th Australian Division pursued the Italians along the coast road, north of the Jebel.

Q105649597.label: Bombing of Sukabumi
Q105649597.desc: 1942 aerial bombing of Java during the WW2
Q105649597.summary: The bombing of Sukabumi was an aerial bombing of the city of Sukabumi, West Java in the Dutch East Indies during the Dutch East Indies campaign of World War II. On the morning of Friday, 6 March 1942, a formation of seven Imperial Japanese aircraft indiscriminately bombed and strafed government buildings, infrastructure, and residential areas, resulting in the deaths of around 70 people and destruction throughout the city.

Q116206525.label: 2023 Dnipro residential building airstrike
Q116206525.desc: 14 January 2023 missile strike during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
Q116206525.summary: On 14 January 2023 at about 3:30 p.m., a Russian Kh-22 missile struck a nine-story residential building in Dnipro, Ukraine, on Naberezhna Peremohy St, 118, Sobornyi District in the right-bank part of the city, destroying one entrance and 236 apartments. On 19 January the official casualty rate was stated as 46 people killed and 80 injured and 11 people reported missing. 14 children were reported injured, and 39 inhabitants were rescued. The destruction left about 400 people homeless.

Q130493373.label: Siege of North Gaza
Q130493373.desc: 2024 military engagement in the Gaza Strip
Q130493373.summary: The siege of North Gaza was an engagement of the Gaza war in the North Gaza Governorate, Gaza Strip, between Israel and Hamas-led Palestinian forces. It began on 5 October 2024 when the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) reinvaded Jabalia and its refugee camp for the first time in months since earlier fighting.

Q2721213.label: Wöhler synthesis
Q2721213.summary: The Wöhler synthesis is the conversion of ammonium cyanate into urea. This chemical reaction was described in 1828 by Friedrich Wöhler. It is often cited as the starting point of modern organic chemistry. Although the Wöhler reaction concerns the conversion of ammonium cyanate, this salt appears only as an (unstable) intermediate.

Q204733.summary: Gerty Theresa Cori was a Czech and American biochemist who in 1947 was the third woman to win a Nobel Prize in science, and the first woman to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, for her role in the "discovery of the course of the catalytic conversion of glycogen".

Q169917.label: graphene
Q169917.summary: Graphene is a variety of the element carbon which occurs naturally in small amounts. In graphene, the carbon forms a sheet of interlocked atoms as hexagons one carbon atom thick. The result resembles the face of a honeycomb. When many hundreds of graphene layers build up, they are called graphite.

Q1606589.label: Henry Calvert Simons
Q1606589.summary: Henry Calvert Simons was an American economist at the University of Chicago. A protégé of Frank Knight, his antitrust and monetarist models influenced the Chicago school of economics. He was a founding author of the Chicago plan for monetary reform that found broad support in the years following the 1930s Depression, which would have abolished the fractional-reserve banking system, which Simons viewed to be inherently unstable.
